newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady, Med stays firm.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady, Med stays firm.

text.p: Mediterranean crude tanker rates remained firm on Monday after soaring last week on an acute shortage of ships and heavy demand, brokers said.

Up to W160 was reported fixed for 80,000 tonne cross-Med trips in fairly quiet activity, against around W100 a week ago. "There's a slow tone right now but I think activity will pick up later in the week," one broker said.

But an Italian broker said he expected Med rates to soften over the next few days. "(The unusually firm market) is not going to last for long...There will be a big reduction of maybe up to 20 points in the next few days," he said.

Middle East and other long-haul rates were also steady in a slow start to the week. Mideast/west voyages for 250,000 tonne very large crude carriers (VLCCs) were little changed at W55, with trips to Japan at W65 and to Singapore at about W57.5, brokers said.

Transatlantic rates were likewise little changed, with both North Sea/USAC and West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs at W62.5 and 130,000 tonners at W95. "There's enough enquiry and tonnage to keep the market broadly balanced for now," one broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont crude cargoes remained at W120 for 80,000 tonne vessels, with 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes steady at W195 on this route and W190 in the Med.
Caribs/U.S. Gulf 70,000 tonners were steady at W165, while 50,000 fuel oil cargoes remained at around W180.
